hypothesis: Request257 shows that causal current-minute dynamics transform pullback entry-value prediction from nearly random to materially informative. A recurrent controller using that minute-state representation should improve the economics of the structural 2% pullback policy.
state: Request257 baseline state plus current minute dynamics and causal current-minus-first-post-HOT minute deltas; no one-second features

models.value: regression of fixed current-state entry value, fit May5-7 with additive bias calibration on May8
models.positive: P(fixed current-state entry value > 0), fit May5-7
models.severe: P(fixed current-state entry value <= -2%), fit May5-7

policy: After the structural 2% pullback trigger, recurrently ENTER at the first state where calibrated predicted value > 0, positive probability >= 0.5, and severe-loss probability < 0.5. Otherwise WAIT. If the 10-minute window ends, remain in cash.
forbidden: using May11-20 outcomes to fit, calibrate, or tune thresholds
using one-second features in this request
tuning the 2% pullback, 0.5 positive, or 0.5 severe thresholds after seeing development outcomes
choosing the best future entry state
next_if_pass: Freeze the minute-state controller and audit its historical one-second aggregate execution support before opening any new holdout.
next_if_fail: Inspect whether the informative minute-state ranking can be converted into policy value with a calibrated ranking/relative decision rule rather than an absolute zero boundary.
